steps.action:
# The Last Light

Every night, Thomas climbed 127 steps.

He knew the number because he'd counted them the first night, forty years ago, when his hands were steady and his knees didn't argue. He still counted them now. It was a habit. A prayer, almost.

The ships rarely came anymore. GPS had made him something of a joke, he supposed. But Thomas lit the lamp anyway, watching the beam sweep across black water, reaching for something it could never quite touch.

One February night, a small boat appeared — engine dead, listing badly in the swells.

He grabbed his radio. Sent the coordinates. Kept the light turning.

By morning, three fishermen stood in his doorway, soaking wet, smelling of the sea, shaking his hand and crying.

Thomas made coffee. He didn't know what to say.

He never did.

He just climbed the steps.
